rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq says the gathering of a group from every community refers to the Return, since the final Resurrection gathers everyone.
rows.anchor: إنها في الرجعة أيحشر الله في القيامة من كل أمة فوجا ويدع الباقين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī notes that Shiʿi reports about the Return are very numerous.
rows.anchor: وأخبار الرجعة من طرق الشيعة كثيرة جدا

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One reported explanation identifies the trumpet as a horn blown like a bugle, an image also found in hadith.
rows.anchor: وقيل هو قرن ينفخ فيه شبه البوق وقد ورد ذلك في الحديث

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A report traced to the Prophet says those exempted from fear are the martyrs, who will not be frightened that day.
rows.anchor: يعني الشهداء فإنهم لا يفزعون في ذلك اليوم وروي ذلك في خبر مرفوع

rows.speaker: القمي
rows.claim: Al-Qummī glosses God’s perfecting all things as God’s act of making each thing firm and complete.
rows.anchor: فعل الله الذي أحكم كل شيء

rows.speaker: القمي
rows.claim: Al-Qummī interprets the good deed as allegiance to ʿAlī and the evil deed as hostility toward him.
rows.anchor: الحسنة والله ولاية أمير المؤمنين عليه السلام والسيئة والله عداوته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He classifies the allegiance interpretation as an application of the verse, not its exegesis, while allowing that related reports may fit what follows.
rows.anchor: وهو من الجري وليس بتفسير وهناك روايات كثيرة في هذا المضمون ربما أمكن حملها على ما سيأتي

rows.speaker: جعفر بن محمد عليه السلام
rows.claim: Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq distinguishes worship for reward, worship from fear of Hell, and worship from love, which he describes as the worship of the noble.
rows.anchor: إن الناس يعبدون الله على ثلاثة أوجه فطبقة يعبدونه رغبة في ثوابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report’s reasoning makes the good deed loving allegiance: the servant’s will is effaced in God’s will, and God takes charge of the servant.
rows.anchor: الولاية التي هي عبادته تعالى من طريق المحبة الموجبة لفناء إرادة العبد في إرادته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is one sense of ʿAlī’s guardianship; as its first opener in the community, he explains many reports identifying the good deed with his allegiance.
rows.anchor: وهذا أحد معنيي ولاية علي عليه السلام فهو عليه السلام صاحب الولاية وأول فاتح لهذا الباب من الامة

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
rows.claim: A report from Kaʿb ibn ʿUjrah identifies the good deed as professing God’s oneness and the evil deed as associating partners, saying one saves and the other ruins.
rows.anchor: يعني بها شهادة أن لا إله إلا الله، ومن جاء بالسيئة يعني بها الشرك يقال هذه تنجي وهذه تردي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He says this interpretation is transmitted in varied forms and must include the religious rulings entailed by monotheism, or their legislation would be pointless.
rows.anchor: وينبغي تقييد تفسير الحسنة بلا إله إلا الله بسائر الأحكام الشرعية التي هي من لوازم التوحيد

rows.speaker: القمي
rows.claim: Al-Qummī identifies the sacred town in the command to worship its Lord as Mecca.
rows.anchor: في قوله تعالى { إنما أمرت أن أعبد رب هذه البلدة الذي حرمها } قال مكة

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
rows.claim: On the conquest of Mecca, the Prophet removed its images and declared its game, trees, and grass protected; ʿAbbās requested and received an exception for idhkhir grass used for graves and houses.
rows.anchor: فهي حرام بحرام الله إلى يوم القيامة لا ينفر صيدها ولا يعضد شجرها ولا يختلي خلالها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī notes that the report on Mecca’s sanctity is also transmitted through Sunni sources.
rows.anchor: وهو مروي من طرق أهل السنة أيضا

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿūd reports a distinction in Qurʾānic wording: one phrase about God’s not overlooking deeds has a tāʾ reading, while the phrase addressed to the Prophet’s Lord has yāʾ.
rows.anchor: قال ما كان في القرآن { وما الله بغافل عما تعملون } بالتاء، وما كان { وما ربك بغافل عما يعملون } بالياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This section recounts events after Moses reached maturity that led him to leave Egypt for Midian.
rows.anchor: فيه ذكر بعض ما وقع بعد بلوغه أشده فأدى إلى خروجه من مصر وقصده مدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The city is Egypt; Moses entered it from outside when its people were inattentive.
rows.anchor: لا ريب أن المدينة التي دخلها على حين غفلة من أهلها هي مصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The later report of a man running from the far end of the city supports the inference that Pharaoh’s palace was outside it.
rows.anchor: ويؤيد ما ذكرنا ما سيأتي من قوله { وجاء من أقصى المدينة رجل يسعى }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The city’s time of inattention is when people return indoors and markets and streets are empty, such as midday or the middle of the night.
rows.anchor: كالظهيرة وأواسط الليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two men were quarrelling and striking one another.
rows.anchor: أي يتنازعان ويتضاربان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Israelite belonged to Moses’ religious party, which traced itself to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob but retained little beyond the name and outwardly worshipped Pharaoh; the opposing man was a Copt, an enemy of Israelites.
rows.anchor: فإن بني إسرائيل كانوا ينتسبون يومئذ إلى آبائهم إبراهيم وإسحاق ويعقوب عليهم السلام في دينهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses’ fear that the Egyptians would kill him for an earlier offense also supports identifying the opponent as a Copt.
rows.anchor: ومن الشاهد أيضا على كون هذا الرجل قبطيا قوله في موضع آخر يخاطب ربه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Israelite asked Moses to support him against his Coptic enemy; istighātha means seeking aid, from ghawth, meaning help.
rows.anchor: الإستغاثة الاستنصار من الغوث بمعنى النصرة أي طلب الإسرائيلي من موسى أن ينصره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wakz means thrusting, pushing, or striking with the gathered hand; the pronouns refer to the opposing man, whom Moses struck and killed.
rows.anchor: والوكز - على ما ذكره الراغب وغيره - الطعن والدفع والضرب بجمع الكف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qadāʾ means judgment, and saying Moses finished the man’s affair is a euphemism for his death.
rows.anchor: والقضاء هو الحكم والقضاء عليه كناية عن الفراغ من أمره بموته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses’ blow killed the Copt by accident; an intentional killing would have been expressed with the word for killing.
rows.anchor: وكان قتل خطأ ولو لا ذلك لكان من حق الكلام أن يعبر بالقتل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase ‘this is Satan’s work’ points to the hostility and fight that culminated in the Copt’s death; min can mean kind or origin.
rows.anchor: و { من } ابتدائية تفيد معنى الجنس أو نشوئية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan stirred enmity and fighting, drawing Moses into the conflict and the killing, which exposed him to grave danger.
rows.anchor: فإنه هو الذي أوقع العداوة والبغضاء بينهما وأغرى على الاقتتال حتى أدى ذلك إلى مداخلة موسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses knew the killing would become known and that the Copts, led by Pharaoh and his chiefs, would retaliate against him and anyone involved.
rows.anchor: وقد كان يعلم أن الواقعة لا تبقى خفية مكتومة وأن القبط سيثورون عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses realized his mistaken blow had put him in danger; he attributes the misstep to Satan because God guides only to truth and what is right.
rows.anchor: أخطأ فيما فعله من الوكز الذي أورده مورد الهلكة ولا ينسب الوقوع في الخطأ إلى الله سبحانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The accidental blow was not a sin: Moses was defending an Israelite against an unjust unbeliever, though Satan can also lead people into non-sinful mistakes that cause hardship, as with Adam and his wife.
rows.anchor: وإن لم يكن معصية منه لوقوعه خطأ وكون دفاعه عن الإسرائيلي دفعا لكافر ظالم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the event Satan’s work expresses Moses’ rejection and regret over the fight that caused the killing and grave danger.
rows.anchor: انزجار منه عما وقع من الاقتتال المؤدي إلى قتل القبطي ووقوعه في عظيم الخطر وندم منه على ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses calls the act Satanic misguidance, meaning an error in judgment and course with dire consequences, not a culpable sin; his answer to Pharaoh later calls it misguidance.
rows.anchor: سوء التدبير وضلال السعي يسوقه إلى عاقبة وخيمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses’ confession of wronging himself means that he placed himself in danger; he asks God to remove the consequences and save him from Pharaoh and his people, as the later account says God rescued him from grief.
rows.anchor: اعتراف منه عند ربه بظلمه نفسه حيث أوردها مورد الخطر وألقاها في التهلكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses’ plea for forgiveness resembles Adam and his wife’s confession that they wronged themselves.
rows.anchor: وهذا الاعتراف بالظلم وسؤال المغفرة نظير ما وقع من آدم وزوجه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preferred reading takes bi-mā as causal: because God bestowed grace, Moses undertakes not to assist criminals; this avoids making him swear by something other than God.
rows.anchor: والوجه الأول هو الأوجه لأن المراد بقوله { بما أنعمت علي }

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One view takes the bāʾ as an oath, with an omitted response meaning ‘I shall repent’ or ‘I shall refrain’ from aiding criminals.
rows.anchor: وقيل الباء للقسم والجواب محذوف والمعنى أقسم بما أنعمت علي لأتوبن

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view treats it as an entreating oath, asking God to show compassion and protect Moses so he will not aid criminals.
rows.anchor: وقيل القسم استعطافى وهو القسم الواقع في الإنشاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He rejects the oath readings because their object would be God’s rescue or forgiveness, an oath by something other than God, which is not used in God’s reported speech.
rows.anchor: ولم يعهد في كلامه تعالى حكايه قسم من غيره بغيره بهذا النحو

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One view calls the Israelite a criminal because he brought another into wrongdoing, or because his appeal led Moses into the killing; this is a figurative attribution of the consequence to its cause.
rows.anchor: من أوقع غيره في الجرم أو من أدت إعانته إلى جرم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view takes the criminals to be Pharaoh and his people and reads Moses’ pledge as ending his association with them; the author says this does not fit the context.
rows.anchor: ورد هذا الوجه الثاني بأنه لا يناسب المقام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses pledges, in gratitude for God’s grace, never to help a criminal commit a crime; the grace is divine guardianship, supported by the description of those God has favored.
rows.anchor: عهد من موسى عليه السلام أن لا يعين مجرما على إجرامه شكرا لله تعالى على ما أنعم عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The favored people follow the straight path and are safe from straying or wrath, which confirms that the grace here is God’s guardianship.
rows.anchor: وهؤلاء أهل الصراط المستقيم مأمونون من الضلال والغضب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The criminals meant are Pharaoh and his followers, not the Israelite: Moses’ defense of the Israelite was not criminal, nor was the accidental blow a sin requiring repentance.
rows.anchor: ومن هنا يظهر أن المراد بالمجرمين أمثال فرعون وقومه دون أمثال الإسرائيلي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses is among the rightly guided and sincere, beyond Satan’s power to mislead, and had been given wisdom and knowledge; he must not act from tribal feeling, misplaced anger, or support for crime.
rows.anchor: وقد نص تعالى أيضا آنفا بأنه آتاه حكما وعلما وأنه من المحسنين ومن المتقين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The three successive ‘he said’ clauses mark different speech acts: judgment, prayer for forgiveness, and a binding commitment.
rows.anchor: وقد كرر { قال } ثلاثا حيث قيل { قال هذا من عمل الشيطان } { قال رب إني ظلمت نفسي } { قال رب بما أنعمت علي } وذلك لاختلاف السياق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase ‘in the city’ indicates Moses stayed there instead of returning to Pharaoh’s palace.
rows.anchor: تقييد { أصبح } بقوله { في المدينة } دليل على أنه بقي في المدينة ولم يرجع إلى قصر فرعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Istisrākh is a loud plea for help, from ṣurākh, a cry; the man who had sought help yesterday now cries out to Moses again.
rows.anchor: والاستصراخ الاستغاثة برفع الصوت من الصراخ بمعنى الصياح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ghawāya means missing the right course, the opposite of sound guidance.
rows.anchor: والغواية إخطاء الصواب خلاف الرشد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses rebukes the Israelite as manifestly erring because continuing to fight people without cause brings only evil.
rows.anchor: لأنه كان يخاصم ويقتتل قوما ليس في مخاصمتهم والمقاومة عليهم إلا الشر كل الشر

rows.speaker: الرضا عليه السلام
rows.claim: In al-Riḍā’s account, Moses killed the enemy by God’s command, while ‘Satan’s work’ refers to the fight between the men, not Moses’ killing.
rows.anchor: فقضى على العدو بحكم الله تعالى ذكره فوكزه فمات، قال هذا من عمل الشيطان يعني الاقتتال الذي وقع بين الرجلين لا ما فعله موسى

rows.speaker: الرضا عليه السلام
rows.claim: Al-Riḍā explains Moses’ wronging himself as entering the city at an unsafe time and his forgiveness plea as asking God to hide him from enemies who might kill him.
rows.anchor: وضعت نفسي غير موضعها بدخول هذه المدينة فاغفر لي أي استرني من أعدائك

rows.speaker: الرضا عليه السلام
rows.claim: Al-Riḍā reads Moses’ pledge as gratitude for the strength God gave him: he will fight criminals with that strength until God is pleased.
rows.anchor: من القوة حتى قتلت رجلا بوكزه فلن أكون ظهيرا للمجرمين بل أجاهدهم بهذه القوة حتى ترضى

rows.speaker: الرضا عليه السلام
rows.claim: Al-Riḍā recounts Moses’ rebuke and intended chastisement of the Israelite for fighting again; the Israelite then accuses Moses of wanting to kill him as he killed a man the day before.
rows.anchor: قاتلت رجلا بالأمس وتقاتل هذا اليوم لأؤدبنك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shift in ‘your Lord creates’ from first-person plural to third-person singular supports and reassures the Prophet: God’s ruling is effective, with no real option to accept or reject it, while the audience denies His lordship.
rows.anchor: والنكتة فيه تأييد النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم وتقويته وتطييب نفسه بإضافة صفة الرب إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Saying ‘Glory be to God’ replaces a pronoun with the explicit name, returning the matter to the transcendent essence that has every perfection and no defect.
rows.anchor: وضع الظاهر موضع المضمر والنكتة فيه إرجاع الأمر إلى الذات المتعالية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iknān means concealment and iʿlām means disclosure; secrets are attributed to the chest because it is treated as their storehouse, while disclosure is attributed to people themselves.
rows.anchor: الإكنان الإخفاء والإعلام الإظهار، ولكون الصدر يعد مخزنا للأسرار نسب الإكنان إلى الصدور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preceding statement is followed by God’s knowledge of hidden and open thoughts to show that He chooses for them with knowledge of their inward and outward sins, purifying them through His wisdom.
rows.anchor: إنما اختار لهم ما اختار لعلمه بما في ظاهرهم وباطنهم من أوساخ الشرك والمعصية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening pronoun refers to ‘your Lord’ in the prior verse; the definite name Allah alludes to a description, and ‘no god but He’ reinforces that only He is divine.
rows.anchor: الضمير في صدر الآية راجع إلى { ربك } في الآية السابقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse completes the argument that God alone may command exclusive worship: He alone is divine and knows their hidden and visible states.
rows.anchor: وهو الإله المستحق للعبادة وحده فيجب عليهم أن يعبدوه وحده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God alone merits worship because every perfection and blessing in both worlds comes from Him, and all praise for them ultimately returns to Him; worship is praise in word or deed.
rows.anchor: والعبادة ثناء بقول أو فعل فهو المعبود المستحق للعبادة وحده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God alone merits worship because He is absolute owner in creation and legislation, and may command His servants to worship Him alone.
rows.anchor: وهو سبحانه مالك في مرحلة التشريع والاعتبار كما أنه مالك في مرحلة التكوين والحقيقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since all return to God for accounting and recompense and He alone judges, He alone must be worshipped and His religion followed.
rows.anchor: وإذ كان هو المحاسب المجازي وحده فهو الذي يجب أن يعبد وحده وله دين يجب أن يتعبد به وحده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘That’ points to God together with His mercy, whose effects include reviving the earth; the distant demonstrative conveys exaltation.
rows.anchor: وفي الإشارة البعيدة تعظيم، والمراد بالموتى موتى الإنسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dead to be revived may mean dead humans alone or humans and other living creatures.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالموتى موتى الإنسان أو الإنسان وغيره من ذوي الحياة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reviving the earth and resurrecting the dead are analogous: both involve life-signs ceasing in something retained and then returning; because earth and plants revive, resurrection is possible by the same rule.
rows.anchor: إذ في كل منهما موت هو سقوط آثار الحياة من شيء محفوظ وحياة هي تجدد تلك الآثار بعد سقوطها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s unlimited power supplies another proof of resurrection: reviving the dead must be possible, or His power would be limited.
rows.anchor: فإن القدرة غير محدودة ولا متناهية فيشمل الإحياء بعد الموت وإلا لزم تقيدها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun ‘it’ refers to the plant inferred from context; the cold wind yellows crops and trees, and the oath’s response says they would then persist in denying God’s gifts.
rows.anchor: ضمير { فرأوه } للنبات المفهوم من السياق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse rebukes their rapid reversal: they rejoice at blessings but soon deny evident gifts when some of what God gave is taken away.
rows.anchor: فإذا لاحت لهم النعمة بادروا إلى الاستبشار، وإذا أخذ بعض ما أنعم الله به من فضله لم يلبثوا

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Other views take ‘it’ as the cloud, which will not rain when yellow, or as the wind, since the word can be masculine or feminine; the author considers both remote.
rows.anchor: والقولان بعيدان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement that the Prophet cannot make the dead hear explains the preceding warning: he should not grieve over people who disbelieve and fail to understand, since they are dead, deaf, and blind; guidance reaches those who believe and grasp the proofs.
rows.anchor: فإنهم موتى وصم وعمي وأنت لا تقدر على إسماعهم وهدايتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He notes that these two verses were already interpreted in Sūrat al-Naml.
rows.anchor: وقد تقدم تفسير الآيتين في سورة النمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because God creates everything, creation entails goodness: each created thing is good insofar as it is created, while sins and relationally bad things are not created insofar as they are bad.
rows.anchor: فينتجان أولا أن الخلقة تلازم الحسن فكل مخلوق حسن من حيث هو مخلوق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The human species began from clay through Adam and his wife, who were created without parents; the contrast with descendants born from fluid supports this reading.
rows.anchor: فالمبدو خلقه من طين هو النوع الذي ينتهي أفراده إلى من خلق من طين من غير تناسل من أب وأم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The contrast between the species’ beginning from clay and later offspring from fluid rules out taking the beginning as an ordinary birth from fluid; otherwise the wording would say he was made from an extract of fluid.
rows.anchor: والمقابلة بين بدء الخلق وبين النسل لا يلائم كون المراد ببدء الخلق بدء خلق الإنسان المخلوق من ماء مهين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Majmaʿ defines sulāla as an extracted essence; semen is called that because it issues from the loins, mahīn means weak or lowly, and thumma marks temporal succession.
rows.anchor: السلالة كما في المجمع الصفوة التي تنسل أي تنزع من غيرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse means that human birth proceeds through separation from an extract of weak or contemptible fluid.
rows.anchor: ثم جعل ولادته بطريق الانفصال من صفوة من ماء ضعيف أو حقير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taswiya means shaping and completing the work; breathing God’s spirit is a metaphor that pictures spirit as breath blown into the formed frame, and its attribution to God is honorific.
rows.anchor: التسوية التصوير وتتميم العمل، وفي قوله { نفخ فيه من روحه } استعارة بالكناية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God formed the human being whose beginning was clay and whose descendants come from lowly fluid, then breathed into him a noble spirit associated with God.
rows.anchor: ثم صور الإنسان المبدو خلقه من الطين والمجعول نسله من سلالة من ماء مهين ونفخ فيه من روح شريف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hearing and sight perceive sensory things, while hearts perceive mental matters, including both particular imaginative and universal rational objects; these are gifts of sense and thought.
rows.anchor: امتنان بنعمة الإدراك الحسي والفكري فالسمع والبصر للمحسوسات والقلوب للفكريات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘You give little thanks’ means that their thanks are few; whether read parenthetically or circumstantially, it rebukes and reproaches them.
rows.anchor: وقوله { قليلا ما تشكرون } أي تشكرون شكرا قليلا، والجملة اعتراضية في محل التوبيخ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shift from speaking of them to addressing them records that God’s universal gifts exceed their thanks, which are insufficient or deficient for most people.
rows.anchor: لتسجيل أن الإنعام الإلهي الشامل للجميع يربو على شكرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The deniers’ objection to resurrection rests on treating it as implausible after bodily decomposition: once dead and scattered, their parts would be indistinguishable from the earth and no trace of them remain.
rows.anchor: حجة من منكري البعث مبنية على الاستبعاد

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: The phrase about being lost in the earth is interpreted either as becoming lost or ruined, like a possession that disappears, or as becoming absent.
rows.anchor: قيل هو الضيعة كما يقال ضلت النعمة أي ضاعت، وقيل هو بمعنى الغيبة
